intro: Hi! Think about your life five or ten years ago: where did you live, how did you get to work or campus, what did you do every weekend? In this lesson you learn used to, the English way to say 'dulu saya …' about habits and situations that are no longer true, plus didn't use to and Did you use to …? Warm-up: finish the sentence 'When I was a student, I used to …'.
teachingNotes: Meaning and form: used to + base verb (the dictionary form: live, go, have) for past habits (repeated actions: I used to take the bus to work) and past states (situations: I used to live in Bandung, She used to have long hair, There used to be a cinema here) that are no longer true now. The form never changes for he/she: she used to work, not *she uses to work or *used to works. Indonesian marks this with 'dulu …' or 'dulu sering …' and doesn't change the verb, so watch for *'I live in Bandung before' or *'Before I work in a bank'.

Spelling and sound: 'used to' is said like 'yuus-tu', with an 's' sound (not the 'z' of used = memakai, 'yuuzd'), and the d disappears into the t of 'to'. Because learners never hear the d, they write *'I use to live…'. Stress it: in a positive sentence it is ALWAYS written used to. Other form errors: *'used to living' (that's 'be used to + -ing', a different expression), *'I was used to live', *'I'm use to'.

There is no present form: 'used to' only talks about the past. Indonesian 'biasanya / saya biasa …' for a habit now is usually + present simple (I usually drink coffee in the morning), not *'I use to drink coffee'. If the learner asks about 'be used to + -ing' (I'm used to the traffic = saya sudah terbiasa), say it's a different expression with a different meaning; don't drill it.

Negatives and questions use did + use to (no d): I didn't use to like coffee. Did you use to live here? Where did you use to work? Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. Link it to didn't go: did already shows the past, so 'use' goes back to its base form; both are still said 'yuus-tu'. Common error: *'didn't used to' / *'Did you used to'. You will see 'didn't used to' in informal native writing, but it's counted as wrong in exams and in this course; give partial credit. 'I never used to …' is a natural alternative for the negative.

Used to vs past simple: the past simple can ALSO describe past habits and states (When I was a child, I lived / used to live in Bandung): never mark the past simple wrong there. used to is impossible for one single event, a total number of times, or a specific moment: *'I used to go to Bali last year' (one trip) → I went to Bali last year; *'I used to visit Japan three times' → I visited Japan three times. But 'three times a year' or 'every Friday' describe a habit, so used to is fine.

Limits: don't teach 'would' for past habits, 'get used to', the past perfect or the present perfect continuous. Keep sentences adult and real (kos, kampus, KRL, ojek online, office, prices in rupiah).

keyPoints.title: used to + base verb: past habits and states
keyPoints.explanation: Use used to + the base verb for things that were true for a long time in the past but are not true now: habits (repeated actions) and states (situations). It's like Indonesian 'dulu …' or 'dulu sering …'. The form is the same for every person: I/she/they used to work. It's said 'yuus-tu' (the d is silent), but in a positive sentence you always write used to, never 'use to'. There's no present form: for habits now, use usually + present simple.

examples.en: I used to live in Bandung, but now I live in Jakarta.
examples.id: Dulu saya tinggal di Bandung, tapi sekarang saya tinggal di Jakarta.

examples.en: Sari used to take the KRL to work every day.
examples.id: Dulu Sari setiap hari naik KRL ke kantor.

examples.en: There used to be a small cinema near my house.
examples.id: Dulu ada bioskop kecil di dekat rumahku.

id.title: used to + kata kerja dasar: kebiasaan dan keadaan di masa lalu
id.explanation: Pakai used to + kata kerja dasar untuk hal yang lama berlaku di masa lalu tapi sekarang tidak lagi: kebiasaan (tindakan yang berulang) dan keadaan (situasi). Mirip 'dulu …' atau 'dulu sering …' dalam bahasa Indonesia. Bentuknya sama untuk semua orang: I/she/they used to work. Dibaca 'yuus-tu' (d tidak terdengar), tapi di kalimat positif selalu ditulis used to, bukan 'use to'. Tidak ada bentuk sekarangnya: untuk kebiasaan sekarang, pakai usually + present simple.

keyPoints.title: didn't use to and Did you use to …?
keyPoints.explanation: Negative: didn't (did not) + use to + base verb: I didn't use to like coffee. Question: Did + subject + use to + base verb: Did you use to live here? With a question word: Where did you use to work? After did there's no -d: did already shows the past, just like didn't go (not 'didn't went'). It still sounds 'yuus-tu'. Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

examples.en: Budi didn't use to work at weekends.
examples.id: Dulu Budi tidak kerja di akhir pekan.

examples.en: Did you use to play football at school? — Yes, I did.
examples.id: Dulu kamu main sepak bola di sekolah? — Ya.

examples.en: What did you use to eat for breakfast in the kos?
examples.id: Dulu waktu di kos kamu sarapan apa?

id.title: didn't use to dan Did you use to …?
id.explanation: Negatif: didn't (did not) + use to + kata kerja dasar: I didn't use to like coffee. Pertanyaan: Did + subjek + use to + kata kerja dasar: Did you use to live here? Dengan kata tanya: Where did you use to work? Setelah did tidak ada -d: did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu, sama seperti didn't go (bukan 'didn't went'). Bunyinya tetap 'yuus-tu'. Jawaban singkat: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

keyPoints.title: used to or past simple?
keyPoints.explanation: For a habit or state over a long period, both are fine: When I was a child, I lived / used to live in Bandung. used to just makes the 'not any more' meaning clearer. But for ONE event, a number of times in total, or a specific moment (yesterday, last Saturday, in 2015), only the past simple works: I went to Bali last year (not 'used to go'). 'Three times a year' or 'every Friday' is a habit, so used to is fine there.

examples.en: I used to go swimming every Sunday.
examples.id: Dulu saya berenang setiap hari Minggu. (kebiasaan: used to atau past simple)
Hari Minggu kemarin saya berenang. (satu kali: hanya past simple)

examples.en: We visited Yogyakarta three times in 2019.
examples.id: Kami mengunjungi Yogyakarta tiga kali pada tahun 2019. (jumlah kali secara total: hanya past simple)

id.title: used to atau past simple?
id.explanation: Untuk kebiasaan atau keadaan dalam waktu yang lama, keduanya benar: When I was a child, I lived / used to live in Bandung. used to hanya membuat arti 'sekarang sudah tidak lagi' lebih jelas. Tapi untuk SATU kejadian, jumlah kali secara total, atau waktu tertentu (yesterday, last Saturday, in 2015), hanya past simple yang benar: I went to Bali last year (bukan 'used to go'). 'Three times a year' atau 'every Friday' itu kebiasaan, jadi used to boleh di situ.

assessment.prompt: Complete with used to and the verb in brackets: When I was at university, I ___ (live) in a kos near the campus.
acceptableAnswers: when i was at university i used to live in a kos near the campus
assessment.rubric: Correct: used to live. 'use to live' = 50 (the d is silent in speech but must be written). 'used to living' = 40 (that's 'be used to + -ing', a different expression). 'used to lived' = 50. 'was used to live' = 30. 'lived' alone = 60 (correct English, but the task asks for used to).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: My father use to smoke, but he stopped five years ago.
acceptableAnswers: my father used to smoke but he stopped five years ago
assessment.rubric: Correct: My father used to smoke, but he stopped five years ago. Only 'used to smoke' written (without the rest of the sentence) = 80. 'uses to smoke' = 20. 'is used to smoke' / 'was used to smoke' = 30. 'used to smoking' = 40. Changing 'stopped' to 'stop' = minus 30. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Make it negative: Rina used to like spicy food.
acceptableAnswers: rina didn't use to like spicy food
rina did not use to like spicy food
rina never used to like spicy food
assessment.rubric: Correct: Rina didn't / did not use to like spicy food ('Rina never used to like spicy food' is also correct). 'didn't used to' = 60 (common in informal writing, but the standard form has no d after did). 'Rina used to not like' = 50. 'Rina didn't like spicy food' = 50 (correct English, but used to is missing). 'Rina not used to like' = 20. 'Rina wasn't used to like' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Make a question: You used to play badminton at school.
acceptableAnswers: did you use to play badminton at school
assessment.rubric: Correct: Did you use to play badminton at school? 'Did you used to play…' = 60 (no d after did). 'Do you use to play…' = 20. 'Were you used to play…' = 20. Statement order with a question mark = 20. 'Did you play badminton at school' = 50 (correct English, but used to is missing).

assessment.prompt: Write the question for this answer, starting with 'Where' and using 'use to': I used to live in Medan, but now I live in Jakarta.
acceptableAnswers: where did you use to live
where did you use to live before
assessment.rubric: Correct: Where did you use to live? 'Where did you used to live' = 60. 'Where you used to live' = 30 (statement order, no did). 'Where do you use to live' = 20. 'Where did you live' = 50 (correct English, but 'use to' is missing). 'Where did you use to live in Medan' = 30 (the answer is already in the question).

assessment.prompt: Correct the verb (keep 'last December'): I used to go to Lombok last December.
acceptableAnswers: i went to lombok last december
last december i went to lombok
assessment.rubric: Correct: I went to Lombok last December. 'Last December' is one trip at one moment, so only the past simple works. 'I use to go' = 0. 'I goed' = 40. 'I go to Lombok last December' = 20. 'I was going to Lombok last December' = 30. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the correct past form of 'meet' (past simple or used to + verb): I ___ my wife at a friend's wedding in 2015.
acceptableAnswers: i met my wife at a friend's wedding in 2015
i met my wife at a friends wedding in 2015
assessment.rubric: Correct: met. You meet your wife for the first time only once, at one wedding in 2015: one event, so past simple. 'used to meet' = 10 (that would mean many times, again and again). 'meeted' = 40 (meet is irregular: met). 'meet' = 20 (not past).

material.title: Dulu, but not now: used to + verb

blocks.text:
When you talk about your life in the past, you often say **dulu …** or **dulu sering …**: *Dulu saya tinggal di Bandung. Dulu saya sering naik KRL.* The meaning is: it was true for a long time, but **it isn't true now**. In English this is **used to + base verb** (the base verb is the dictionary form: *live, go, have, like*).

used to works for two things:
- **habits**: actions you did again and again: *I used to take the KRL to work.*
- **states**: situations that lasted: *I used to live in Bandung. She used to have long hair. There used to be a cinema here.*

The form is the **same for every person**: *I used to, she used to, they used to*. No -s (not 'she uses to') and no -s or -ed on the verb after it (not 'used to works').

id.text:
Saat bercerita tentang hidupmu di masa lalu, kamu sering bilang **dulu …** atau **dulu sering …**: *Dulu saya tinggal di Bandung. Dulu saya sering naik KRL.* Artinya: hal itu lama berlaku, tapi **sekarang sudah tidak lagi**. Dalam bahasa Inggris ini adalah **used to + kata kerja dasar** (kata kerja dasar = bentuk kamus: *live, go, have, like*).

used to dipakai untuk dua hal:
- **kebiasaan**: tindakan yang kamu lakukan berulang-ulang: *I used to take the KRL to work.*
- **keadaan**: situasi yang berlangsung lama: *I used to live in Bandung. She used to have long hair. There used to be a cinema here.*

Bentuknya **sama untuk semua orang**: *I used to, she used to, they used to*. Tanpa -s (bukan 'she uses to') dan kata kerja sesudahnya juga tanpa -s atau -ed (bukan 'used to works').

rows.en: I used to work in a bank, but now I'm a teacher.
rows.id: Dulu saya kerja di bank, tapi sekarang saya guru.

rows.en: Pak Hasan used to drink five cups of coffee a day.
rows.id: Dulu Pak Hasan minum lima cangkir kopi sehari.

rows.en: My kids used to love cartoons. Now they only watch YouTube.
rows.id: Dulu anak-anakku suka sekali film kartun. Sekarang mereka cuma nonton YouTube.

rows.en: There used to be a big market here.
rows.id: Dulu di sini ada pasar besar.
rows.note: there is → there used to be

id.note: there is → there used to be

rows.en: A plate of nasi goreng used to cost 5,000 rupiah.
rows.id: Dulu sepiring nasi goreng harganya 5.000 rupiah.

blocks.text:
Two Indonesian traps:
- Indonesian doesn't change the verb, it only adds *dulu*. So learners say 'I live in Bandung before'. English needs a past form: **I used to live in Bandung.**
- **used to is only for the past.** For a habit **now** (*biasanya, saya biasa …*), use **usually** + present simple: *Saya biasa minum kopi pagi-pagi* = **I usually drink coffee in the morning**, not 'I use to drink coffee'.

id.text:
Dua jebakan untuk penutur bahasa Indonesia:
- Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja, hanya menambah *dulu*. Jadi orang sering bilang 'I live in Bandung before'. Bahasa Inggris perlu bentuk lampau: **I used to live in Bandung.**
- **used to hanya untuk masa lalu.** Untuk kebiasaan **sekarang** (*biasanya, saya biasa …*), pakai **usually** + present simple: *Saya biasa minum kopi pagi-pagi* = **I usually drink coffee in the morning**, bukan 'I use to drink coffee'.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani used to teach English. What does this mean?
options: She taught English in the past, but not now.
blocks.explain: used to = it was true for a long time in the past, but it isn't true now (dulu …, sekarang tidak lagi).

id.prompt: Bu Ani used to teach English. Apa artinya?
id.explain: used to = hal itu lama berlaku di masa lalu, tapi sekarang tidak lagi (dulu …, sekarang tidak lagi).
options: Dia mengajar bahasa Inggris dahulu, tetapi sekarang tidak lagi.
Dia akan segera mengajar bahasa Inggris.

id.title: Dulu, sekarang tidak lagi: used to + kata kerja

material.title: Why people write 'use to' (and why it's wrong)

blocks.text:
Listen to a native speaker and you'll hear **used to** as one quick word: **'yuus-tu'**. Two surprises:
- the **s** sounds like **'s'**, not 'z' (the verb *use* = memakai is said 'yuuz', and *I used my phone* = 'yuuzd');
- the **d disappears**: d and the t of *to* are almost the same sound, so they melt into one 't'.

Because nobody hears the d, many learners write **'I use to live…'**. That's wrong. **In a positive sentence, always write used to**, with d, for every person.

The only place you write *use to* without d is after **did** (*didn't use to, Did you use to…?*): you'll see why in the next section. It sounds exactly the same: 'yuus-tu'.

id.text:
Dengarkan penutur asli dan kamu akan mendengar **used to** seperti satu kata cepat: **'yuus-tu'**. Ada dua kejutan:
- huruf **s** dibaca **'s'**, bukan 'z' (kata kerja *use* = memakai dibaca 'yuuz', dan *I used my phone* = 'yuuzd');
- huruf **d hilang**: bunyi d dan bunyi t di *to* hampir sama, jadi keduanya melebur jadi satu 't'.

Karena d-nya tidak terdengar, banyak pelajar menulis **'I use to live…'**. Itu salah. **Di kalimat positif, selalu tulis used to**, dengan d, untuk semua orang.

Satu-satunya tempat kamu menulis *use to* tanpa d adalah setelah **did** (*didn't use to, Did you use to…?*): alasannya ada di bagian berikutnya. Bunyinya sama persis: 'yuus-tu'.

rows.en: I used to live in a kos.
I used my phone to pay.
rows.note: a different verb: used = memakai, said 'yuuzd'

id.note: kata kerja lain: used = memakai, dibaca 'yuuzd'

rows.en: He used to sell phones online.
rows.note: he used to, not 'he uses to'

id.note: he used to, bukan 'he uses to'

rows.en: I usually take an ojek to work.
rows.id: Biasanya saya naik ojek ke kantor.
rows.note: a habit now: usually, not 'use to'

blocks.text: Don't confuse **used to + verb** with **be used to + -ing**: *I'm used to the traffic. I'm used to getting up early.* That's a different expression that means **sudah terbiasa** (it's about now, and it needs am/is/are). You don't need it in this lesson; just don't mix them: 'I used to living' and 'I was used to live' are wrong.

id.text: Jangan tertukar **used to + kata kerja** dengan **be used to + -ing**: *I'm used to the traffic. I'm used to getting up early.* Itu ungkapan lain yang artinya **sudah terbiasa** (tentang sekarang, dan perlu am/is/are). Kamu belum perlu memakainya di pelajaran ini; yang penting jangan dicampur: 'I used to living' dan 'I was used to live' itu salah.

blocks.prompt: When he lived in Jogja, Dimas ___ to work by bike.
blocks.explain: A positive sentence always has used to (with d) + base verb: used to go. You can't hear the d, but you write it. 'used to going' mixes in 'be used to + -ing', a different expression.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: When he lived in Jogja, Dimas ___ to work by bike.
id.explain: Kalimat positif selalu memakai used to (dengan d) + kata kerja dasar: used to go. d-nya tidak terdengar, tapi tetap ditulis. 'used to going' tercampur dengan 'be used to + -ing', ungkapan yang lain.

id.title: Kenapa orang menulis 'use to' (dan kenapa itu salah)

material.title: didn't use to and Did you use to …?

blocks.text:
Negatives and questions work like the past simple you know: **did** does the work.
- Negative: **didn't (did not) + use to + base verb**: *I didn't use to like coffee.*
- Question: **Did + subject + use to + base verb**: *Did you use to live here?* (the subject = who you ask about: *you, Rina, your parents*)
- With a question word: *Where did you use to work? What did you use to eat?*
- Short answers: **Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.**

Why no d? Remember *I didn't go* (not 'didn't went'): **did already shows the past**, so the next verb goes back to its base form. *used* → **use**. It sounds the same ('yuus-tu'), only the spelling changes.

id.text:
Kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan bekerja seperti past simple yang sudah kamu kenal: **did** yang bekerja.
- Negatif: **didn't (did not) + use to + kata kerja dasar**: *I didn't use to like coffee.*
- Pertanyaan: **Did + subjek + use to + kata kerja dasar**: *Did you use to live here?* (subjek = siapa yang kamu tanyakan: *you, Rina, your parents*)
- Dengan kata tanya: *Where did you use to work? What did you use to eat?*
- Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.**

Kenapa tanpa d? Ingat *I didn't go* (bukan 'didn't went'): **did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu**, jadi kata kerja berikutnya kembali ke bentuk dasar. *used* → **use**. Bunyinya sama ('yuus-tu'), hanya ejaannya yang berubah.

rows.en: Dimas didn't use to cook. Now he cooks every day.
rows.id: Dulu Dimas tidak masak. Sekarang dia masak setiap hari.

rows.en: My office didn't use to have a canteen.
Did your parents use to live in Surabaya? — No, they didn't.
rows.id: Dulu orang tuamu tinggal di Surabaya? — Tidak.

rows.en: Which school did you use to go to?
I never used to read the news. Now I read it every morning.
rows.id: Dulu saya tidak pernah baca berita. Sekarang saya baca setiap pagi.
rows.note: never used to = another way to say didn't use to

id.note: never used to = cara lain untuk bilang didn't use to

blocks.text: You may see **'didn't used to'** or **'Did you used to…?'** in messages or on social media, even from native speakers. In exams, at work and in this course, it counts as a mistake: write **didn't use to** and **Did you use to…?**. With *never*, there's no did, so the d stays: **I never used to…**.

id.text: Kamu mungkin melihat **'didn't used to'** atau **'Did you used to…?'** di chat atau media sosial, bahkan dari penutur asli. Di ujian, di tempat kerja dan di kursus ini, itu dianggap salah: tulis **didn't use to** dan **Did you use to…?**. Dengan *never*, tidak ada did, jadi d-nya tetap: **I never used to…**.

options: Did you used to wear glasses?
Did you use to wear glasses?
Do you use to wear glasses?
blocks.explain: Did + subject + use to (no d, because did already shows the past) + base verb. 'Do you use to' is wrong: used to has no present form.

id.explain: Did + subjek + use to (tanpa d, karena did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu) + kata kerja dasar. 'Do you use to' salah: used to tidak punya bentuk sekarang.

id.title: didn't use to dan Did you use to …?

rows.id: Dulu Rina kerja di sebuah hotel di Bali.
rows.note: a long period: used to or worked

id.note: waktu yang lama: used to atau worked

rows.id: Rina mulai kerja di tempat baru bulan Maret lalu.

rows.en: We used to eat out every Saturday night.
rows.id: Dulu kami makan di luar setiap Sabtu malam.

rows.en: We ate out twice last week.
rows.id: Minggu lalu kami makan di luar dua kali.
rows.note: a total number of times: past simple only

id.note: jumlah kali secara total: hanya past simple

blocks.text: A quick test: can you add **'dulu, sekarang tidak lagi'** and **'berulang-ulang / lama'** to the Indonesian? If yes, used to fits. If the sentence has a date, *yesterday*, *last …*, *… ago* for one event, or a number like *twice*, use the past simple. To say it stopped, English often adds **not any more** (British) or **not anymore** (American): *I don't smoke any more.*

id.text: Tes cepat: apakah kamu bisa menambahkan **'dulu, sekarang tidak lagi'** dan **'berulang-ulang / lama'** ke kalimat Indonesianya? Kalau bisa, used to cocok. Kalau kalimatnya punya tanggal, *yesterday*, *last …*, *… ago* untuk satu kejadian, atau angka seperti *twice* (dua kali), pakai past simple. Untuk bilang sesuatu sudah berhenti, bahasa Inggris sering menambahkan **not any more** (British) atau **not anymore** (Amerika): *I don't smoke any more.*

blocks.prompt: Rina ___ to Japan three times when she worked for that company.
blocks.explain: three times (without 'a year') is a total number of times, counted from start to finish, so only the past simple works: went. 'used to go three times a year' would be a habit.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina ___ to Japan three times when she worked for that company.
id.explain: three times (tanpa 'a year') adalah jumlah kali secara total, dihitung dari awal sampai akhir, jadi hanya past simple yang benar: went. 'used to go three times a year' baru kebiasaan.

resources.title: Past habits: 'used to', 'would' and the past simple
resources.note: A B1–B2 page with two grammar tests. It also teaches 'would' for past habits, which is not in this lesson: you can skip that part.

id.note: Halaman level B1–B2 dengan dua tes tata bahasa. Halaman ini juga mengajarkan 'would' untuk kebiasaan lampau, yang tidak ada di pelajaran ini: bagian itu boleh dilewati.

resources.title: Used to
resources.note: A reference page with many examples of used to, didn't use to and questions. It's above this lesson's level and also covers 'would' and question tags.

id.note: Halaman referensi dengan banyak contoh used to, didn't use to dan pertanyaan. Levelnya di atas pelajaran ini dan juga membahas 'would' serta question tag.

flashcards.back: I used to live in Bandung.

flashcards.front: Negatif: He used to work late.
flashcards.back: He didn't use to work late. (no d after did)

flashcards.front: Pertanyaan: She used to play the guitar.
flashcards.back: Did she use to play the guitar?
I usually get up at five. (not 'I use to')

flashcards.front: Satu kejadian: Kemarin saya ke dokter gigi.
flashcards.back: I went to the dentist yesterday. (past simple only)
There used to be a cinema here.

id.intro: Hai! Coba ingat hidupmu lima atau sepuluh tahun yang lalu: dulu kamu tinggal di mana, naik apa ke kantor atau kampus, apa yang kamu lakukan setiap akhir pekan? Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar used to, cara bahasa Inggris untuk bilang 'dulu saya …' tentang kebiasaan dan keadaan yang sekarang sudah tidak berlaku, juga didn't use to dan Did you use to …? Pemanasan: lanjutkan kalimat 'When I was a student, I used to …'.
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa ditulis 'used to' kalau d-nya tidak terdengar?
Kenapa 'didn't use to', bukan 'didn't used to'?
Boleh bilang 'I lived in Bandung' daripada 'I used to live in Bandung'?

assessment.ut-1: Lengkapi dengan used to dan kata kerja dalam kurung: When I was at university, I ___ (live) in a kos near the campus.
assessment.ut-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: My father use to smoke, but he stopped five years ago.
assessment.ut-3: Ubah ke kalimat negatif: Rina used to like spicy food.
assessment.ut-4: Ubah ke kalimat tanya: You used to play badminton at school.
assessment.ut-5: Tulis pertanyaan dalam bahasa Inggris untuk jawaban ini, mulai dengan 'Where' dan pakai 'use to': I used to live in Medan, but now I live in Jakarta.
assessment.ut-6: Perbaiki kata kerjanya (tetap pakai 'last December'): I used to go to Lombok last December.
assessment.ut-7: Lengkapi dengan bentuk lampau yang benar dari 'meet' (past simple atau used to + kata kerja): I ___ my wife at a friend's wedding in 2015.
